- Affected part: A single tomato leaf (upper surface visible)

- **Early Blight / Target Spot**: Both require distinct brown lesions with concentric rings — not present here
- **Septoria Leaf Blotch**: Small circular gray-centered lesions with dark borders — not visible
- **Bacterial diseases**: Typically produce water-soaked, dark-bordered lesions — not seen
- **Powdery Mildew**: White powdery coating on leaf surfaces — not apparent
- **Verticillium Wilt**: V-shaped margin lesions, vascular streaking — not matching
- **Leaf_Mold**: "Pale greenish-yellow spots, usually less than 1/4 inch with no definite margins, form on the upper sides of leaves" — this matches closely. The pale yellow irregular patches with indistinct margins on the upper leaf surface are characteristic. The velvety olive-brown mold would appear on the underside (not visible here).

The diffuse, pale greenish-yellow spots without defined margins on the upper leaf surface is the hallmark presentation of Leaf Mold.
